integration_issues.flow: File picker on web — expo-file-system File.bytes() fallback
integration_issues.issue: On web preview, `new File(asset.uri).bytes()` throws (caught silently) so head bytes + textSample stay null. Consequence: the URL inside the PDF ('https://pay-invoice-now.top/abc') is not extracted, file-links card is not rendered, and state is Patrolling (F10 via MIME=application/pdf) instead of Ears up (F05). No crash — graceful degradation as spec allowed. On real device (iOS/Android) the bytes path will run and URL extraction + link hand-off will trigger. Fallback branch is per the review request note; documenting behavior for the record.

action_items: OPTIONAL (already documented): Consider using a web-friendly bytes read path (e.g. asset.file / fetch(asset.uri).arrayBuffer()) inside file.tsx pick() so web preview can also detect embedded URLs and produce Ears up F05 for invoice PDFs with pay links. Not required — spec allowed fallback.

Backend regression note (pre-existing, unrelated to Gate 6): test_apollo_backend.py::test_intel_status / test_intel_check_unknown / test_intel_check_batch_mixed now fail because Google Safe Browsing key is 'ok' (not 'auth_error') and unknown URLs are now graded 'clean' (not 'unknown', full coverage instead of partial). These are stale test expectations. Update assertions in test_apollo_backend.py OR treat as improved coverage. Not blocking.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L510-524: POST /api/patrol/events now correctly upserts via find-first + try/except DuplicateKeyError fallback. Under real concurrent races (verified 5x threads + asyncio.gather), both paths converge to a single row and 200 status. Clean fix for iteration-12 race.

server.py L521-524: The `except DuplicateKeyError` block re-fetches after $set — good, but consider `find_one_and_update(..., upsert=True, return_document=AFTER)` as a single-round-trip idempotent alternative that avoids the initial find_one probe entirely.

file.tsx L64-70: The try/catch around `new File(asset.uri).bytes()` swallows the web-side unsupported-op silently (comment 'web or unreadable: fall back to name + MIME'). This is intentional and matches the review spec's graceful-fallback requirement — but a console.debug in dev would help future debugging.

fileAnalysis.ts L74-75: F01 title uses `${(inner || ext).toUpperCase()}` for the disguised-executable message — correctly says 'not really a PDF' when name='Statement.pdf.exe' (inner=pdf, ext=exe). Nice.

fileAnalysis.ts L87 F10: `f.source === 'nearby' ? 'ears_up' : 'resting'` — good source-aware nuance. Note that a legitimate PDF from a 'message' source stays resting (F10), which is what the acceptance test expects for MeetingAgenda.pdf from a known sender.

rca_of_issue: Iteration-12 bug (POST /api/patrol/events → 500 DuplicateKeyError on Gate-3+Gate-5 event merge) is FIXED in iteration 13. Root cause: server previously did insert_one on a unique-indexed collection (device_id_1_event_id_1) which raced when two concurrent POSTs for the same (device_id, event_id) both saw find_one=None and both called insert_one. Fix (server.py L510-524): wrap the insert_one in try/except DuplicateKeyError; on catch, run update_one($set) + re-fetch and return the updated doc as if inserted. Verified with 3 dedicated tests (2-way asyncio, 5-way threadpool, sequential update). No other backend regressions introduced. Frontend picker-on-web behavior noted (graceful name+MIME fallback) is documented as per-spec and does not block acceptance.
